messages.subject: rstan_2.6.0.tar.gz fails to build under Mac OS Yosemite
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to build RStan for Mac OS. Here is the session info:

R version 3.1.3 (2015-03-09)
Platform: x86_64-apple-darwin13.4.0 (64-bit)
Running under: OS X 10.10.1 (Yosemite)

locale:
[1] en_US.UTF-8/en_US.UTF-8/en_US.UTF-8/C/en_US.UTF-8/en_US.UTF-8

attached base packages:
[1] stats     graphics  grDevices utils     datasets  methods   base     

other attached packages:
[1] Rcpp_0.11.5   inline_0.3.13

loaded via a namespace (and not attached):
[1] tools_3.1.3

Everything seems to start normally:

* installing *source* package ‘rstan’ ...
** package ‘rstan’ successfully unpacked and MD5 sums checked
** libs
clang++ -I/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources/include -DNDEBUG -I"../inst/include/stansrc"   -I"../inst/include" ...

Here is the first error:
/usr/local/include/boost/utility/result_of.hpp:189:46: error: too few template arguments for class template 'result'
struct result_of_nested_result : F::template result<FArgs>

and finally:
18 errors generated.
make: *** [gm__grammars__expression07_grammar_inst.o] Error 1
ERROR: compilation failed for package ‘rstan’
* removing ‘/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.1/Resources/library/rstan’

Here is my clang info:
Apple LLVM version 6.0 (clang-600.0.56) (based on LLVM 3.5svn)
Target: x86_64-apple-darwin14.0.0
Thread model: posix

Any hints are much appreciated.

Eric

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] rstan_2.6.0.tar.gz fails to build under Mac OS Yosemite
parts:
Did you have Stan installed previously? And if so,
have you made sure to stop and restart R? It looks like
a library mismatch.

Also, how much memory do you have?

If that's not it, could you send us the entire dump of
the session, not just the first error you get?

And someone with more knowledge of R than me will need to
help out.

Thanks,

- Bob

parts:
It picks up a local version of Boost

In file included from gm__grammars__expression07_grammar_inst.cpp:1:

In file included from /usr/local/include/boost/spirit/include/qi.hpp:16:
In file included from /usr/local/include/boost/spirit/home/qi.hpp:14:
In file included from /usr/local/include/boost/spirit/home/qi/action.hpp:14:
In file included from /usr/local/include/boost/spirit/home/qi/action/action.hpp:14:
In file included from /usr/local/include/boost/spirit/home/qi/meta_compiler.hpp:14:
In file included from /usr/local/include/boost/spirit/home/support/meta_compiler.hpp:16:
In file included from /usr/local/include/boost/spirit/include/phoenix_limits.hpp:11:
In file included from /usr/local/include/boost/phoenix/core/limits.hpp:26:
In file included from /usr/local/include/boost/proto/proto_fwd.hpp:28:
/usr/local/include/boost/utility/result_of.hpp:189:46: error: too few template arguments for class template 'result'

If you are commenting out the part where it installs BH, then you need to have the same version of Boost as BH in /usr/local/include.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] rstan_2.6.0.tar.gz fails to build under Mac OS Yosemite
parts:
You need an earlier version of Boost that doesn't use Boost 1.58.
There have been several messages on the list over the last couple
days on how to do this.

BH pulled the rug out from under us by upgrading to Boost 1.58.
Ironically, BH never upgrading is what had us pinned at Boost 1.55 previously.

We're working on tracking down all the fixes needed. We've got
it nailed down for everything but Windows and as soon as we workaround
all the Windows failures with Boost 1.58, we'll release a patched
RStan.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] rstan_2.6.0.tar.gz fails to build under Mac OS Yosemite
parts:
You need an older version of the package BH that is before
they moved to Boost 1.58 (they used to be at Boost 1.55).

- Bob

> On May 28, 2015, at 3:30 PM, Andrew Azman <andre...@gmail.com> wrote:

> I am having the same issue and trying to follow others solutions by adding an older version of boost to `/usr/local/include' but this doesn't seem to do it. Any ideas?

>
> On Wed, May 27, 2015 at 10:22 PM Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
> You need an earlier version of Boost that doesn't use Boost 1.58.
> There have been several messages on the list over the last couple
> days on how to do this.
>
> BH pulled the rug out from under us by upgrading to Boost 1.58.
> Ironically, BH never upgrading is what had us pinned at Boost 1.55 previously.
>
> We're working on tracking down all the fixes needed. We've got
> it nailed down for everything but Windows and as soon as we workaround
> all the Windows failures with Boost 1.58, we'll release a patched
> RStan.
>
> - Bob
